issue.description:
Verified 2026-07-30. tests/integration/fixtures/passing-suite and tests/integration/fixtures/failing-suite (added in commit d67dfa5, bf-82k4: create integration test fixture with passing and failing test suites) are committed as git submodule links (gitlink, mode 160000):

  git ls-files -s tests/integration/fixtures/
  160000 2c52c68... tests/integration/fixtures/failing-suite
  160000 c7bbce9... tests/integration/fixtures/passing-suite

There is no .gitmodules file anywhere in the repo registering these as submodules. Confirmed by fresh-clone test:  of this repo into a scratch dir leaves both directories completely empty (no Cargo.toml, no lib.rs, no .git) — git has no URL to fetch the submodule content from without a .gitmodules entry.

Impact: tests/integration.rs (the suite proving the walking-skeleton exit criterion, bf-4kw/bf-1f9/bf-1p02/bf-1ees) calls run_cargo_test("passing-suite") and depends on these fixtures containing real cargo projects. On any genuinely fresh clone — a new NEEDLE worker checkout, a CI runner, a future contributor —  will fail (fixture dirs empty) or silently no-op depending on how the test resolves the missing path. This has not been caught so far because the current checkout has uncommitted local content sitting in those directories from whenever they were first populated, and the cargo-remote shim on this box falls back to local-only execution whenever there are uncommitted changes (which this repo currently always has), so a truly clean-tree remote/CI run of this suite has apparently never happened.

This is the walking skeletons own proof-of-correctness suite for a project whose entire purpose is never losing a test result / never silently skipping — worth fixing before Phase 1a closes out further, since it undermines the credibility of every quality gates passed bead closure that depended on tests/integration.rs actually exercising these fixtures.

Fix is one of: (a) properly register them as real git submodules with a .gitmodules pointing at real remotes (probably wrong for throwaway test fixtures), (b) remove the gitlink and commit the fixture files as normal tracked files (matches how tests/fixture/ already does it — that directory IS committed as plain files, only tests/integration/fixtures/* are the broken gitlinks), or (c) generate the fixtures at test-setup time instead of committing them. Reference: tests/integration.rs top-of-file comment describing the two fixtures; tests/fixture/ for the correct committed-plain-files pattern already used elsewhere in this same repo.
issue.title: Integration test fixtures are broken git submodule links with no .gitmodules — empty dirs on fresh clone
